item.title: Kyle Whittingham Makes Bold Statement Following Michigan’s Stunning Victory
item.description: Kyle Whittingham celebrated his 67th birthday Saturday with a victory he won’t soon forget. Michigan’s embattled head coach watched his Wolverines stun previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime, securing bowl eligibility and delivering one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. But when Whittingham stepped in front of reporters following the game, he wasn’t interested in making the moment about himself. Instead, he immediately turned his attention to Michigan’s seniors, who had just played their final game at The Big House. Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham reacts to a play against UCLA during the first half at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kyle Whittingham Delivers Emotional Message About Michigan Seniors For Whittingham, Saturday’s Senior Day victory meant considerably more than another win in the standings. He explained that sending Michigan’s seniors out with a victory had been a major focus throughout the week. “Well, first of all, I’m so thrilled for the seniors, the guys that played their last game in The Big House,” Whittingham said. “That was the point of emphasis all week long, was to send those guys out the right way.” The veteran coach then praised the players for sticking together through what has been an incredibly frustrating season. Despite Michigan’s struggles, Whittingham made it clear that his appreciation for the team hasn’t wavered. “I’m so proud of those guys, love this football team, a bunch of great guys, great guys to coach, to be around, and it was, like I said, a big point of emphasis. And to see that happen was so gratifying to see that.” Michigan entered Saturday’s matchup needing one more victory to become bowl eligible, a difficult assignment against an undefeated UCLA squad. The Wolverines had been searching for their sixth win , but they picked quite a moment to finally get it. It was a fitting conclusion to Senior Day, particularly considering the number of close games Michigan had failed to finish earlier in the year. item.title: CBA breezes into the Class AA state semifinals after routing Valley Central
item.description: CBA senior JT Vogel, left, and sophomore Jacob Turner celebrate after Vogel blocked a punt and Turner returned it for a touchdown during the Class AA state quarterfinals against Valley Central on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) COLONIE - One carry, one touchdown. A second carry, another touchdown. A third carry, a third touchdown. Then, the offense for the Christian Brothers Academy football team actually slowed down during its fourth possession Saturday, as the Brothers required three plays to reach the end zone that time. The state's No. 3-ranked Class AA squad displayed its overall prowess once again, this time blasting Section 9 champion Valley Central 69-6 in state quarterfinal play at Colonie High School. CBA (12-0) ran the ball four times during the opening quarter and scored touchdowns on each attempt. In all, the Brothers amassed 263 yards of offense over six plays in the first quarter, which ended with the Brothers ahead 28-0. "It felt good to play like that," said CBA junior two-way standout Jack Hulett, who was named his team's Offensive Player of the Game. "Coach (Bobby) Burns and the rest of the staff got us prepared pretty well for what we needed to do. We came out and played hard." The Brothers produced a resounding 61-14 triumph over Saratoga Springs in the Section 2 Class AA Super Bowl to secure a fifth sectional title since 2021. There was absolutely zero letdown Saturday, as CBA senior running back Tommy Toher opened the scoring festivities by dashing 80 yards for a touchdown on the first play from scrimmage. That score started a streak of three consecutive plays from scrimmage that saw the CBA offense score a touchdown. "Monday, we flipped the script from Saratoga to this game," Hulett said. "This is a highly motivated group. They are locked in," Burns said. "They want to get back to the (JMA Wireless Dome in Syracuse) for the state final and want to get it done. That is the motivation." Hulett, a junior who stars at receiver and safety, proceeded to help make it 21-0 as he generated touchdown runs covering 79 and 60 yards, respectively. Toher's second touch of the game resulted in a 4-yard touchdown run with 1:33 left in the first quarter. The Brothers added four more touchdowns in the second quarter to lead 55-0 at intermission. "When we execute, we have special players that can do special things," Burns said. "All the work we have put in is paying off. We are now looking to next week and trying to get better in order to reach the Dome," Hulett said. The CBA starters had the second half off. The Brothers' reserves moved the ball efficiently over the final 24 minutes, featuring some strong runs by Brady Munsinger and Tyrone Barrow. Jacob Turner, a sophomore who scooped up a blocked punt and scored a touchdown in the second quarter, returned a kickoff 88 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. item.title: Blackhawks Captain Connor Bedard Will Undergo Right Shoulder Surgery
item.description: The Chicago Blackhawks should be riding high after earning their first road win of the 2026-27 regular season against the Calgary Flames on Saturday night. But it’s hard to celebrate too much when the star player and team captain is now facing another extended absence. After Saturday’s win, general manager Kyle Davidson told the media that Connor Bedard has decided to undergo surgery to repair his right shoulder. Bedard, the Blackhawks team doctors, and outside experts have recently been weighing the pros and cons of rehab vs. surgery for his latest injury . We now know his choice. Breaking: Connor Bedard is getting shoulder surgery, Kyle Davidson says. — Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) November 22, 2026 Bedard suffered the injury in Tuesday’s 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs , while battling with Leafs center Nick Paul at the faceoff circle. Last December, Bedard injured his right shoulder in similar circumstances, getting tangled up with then-St. Louis Blues captain Brayden Schenn while trying to win a faceoff. Bedard chose rehab over surgery last winter and returned to the Blackhawks roughly four weeks later, missing 12 games. But after suffering the same injury again, his second serious right shoulder injury in 11 months, the risk of re-injury or doing further damage without surgery appeared to be too much. The 21-year-old will undergo surgery this week, marking his second shoulder procedure in under five months. Bedard had left shoulder surgery on July 8 stemming from a freak accident during offseason training in Vancouver. He returned to the Blackhawks on Oct. 13 after missing the first six games of the 2026-27 season. Davidson told the traveling media that Bedard’s upcoming right shoulder surgery will likely be the same procedure he had on his left shoulder in July. Dr. Peter Millett, the surgeon who repaired Bedard’s left shoulder this past summer, will also repair his right shoulder. Bedard’s return timeline won’t be determined until after surgery, per Davidson, but it will likely be between 3-4 months. For his left shoulder, Bedard was initially given a four-month recovery timeline, but he returned in just over three months. That puts Bedard on track to potentially return in mid-to-late February, at the earliest. However, considering this will be his second serious procedure in such a short stretch, the Blackhawks will presumably be extra cautious with the face of the franchise. While it’s another devastating development for the Blackhawks early this season, and as difficult as the decision must have been for Bedard, he made the correct one. Electing to do rehab again and returning with a banged-up shoulder is a risk neither he nor the Blackhawks could afford. A third injury could have led to dire consequences and created serious long-term issues. As the prized jewel of the rebuild, Bedard had to nip this in the bud, right here, right now. item.description: STATE COLLEGE, Pa. — Rutgers fulfilled Greg Schiano’s promise that it would win a game that no one expected after all. Behind a starting quarterback playing with three broken ribs and a defense that ranked among the worst in the country, the Scarlet Knights stunned Penn State in a 25-24 victory that snapped a decades-long losing streak and rewarded the school’s decision to maintain its maligned head coach for the eighth season of his second stint. And Rutgers (3-8, 2-6) did so in unbelievable fashion, erasing a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit with two gutsy drives, including a game-tying 11-play, 67-yard odyssey in the final 3 minutes and 28 seconds, capped off by what will go down as one of the most iconic plays in recent Rutgers football history. The Scarlet Knights elected to go for two, and quarterback AJ Surace completed one of the gutsiest performances in program history with a pass to running back Clay Thevenin, who ran into the end zone for the victory. item.title: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb punished by the NFL before Titans game
item.description: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb punished by the NFL before Titans game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NFL season is already reaching its later stages, and it's crunch time for the Dallas Cowboys . If this team wants to make the playoffs, it's going to have to start winning and keep it up for the rest of the season. That starts Sunday when the Cowboys take on the Titans at home. Now, one of the team's biggest offensive stars, CeeDee Lamb, is getting punished by the NFL ahead of the matchup. CeeDee Lamb receives the biggest fine of the week after helmet-related penalty against the 49ers Every week during the season, the NFL announces fines on Saturday for games played the week before. So, the league's Week 10 punishments are out. "The rules are intended to protect the players from unnecessary risk, promote player safety and emphasize sportsmanship and respect of teammates, opponents, coaches, officials and fans," the NFL notes on its official website . As you can probably guess, Lamb was slapped with a fine this week for actions during the team's 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . The NFL is fining Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb $23,882 for unnecessary roughness after he was flagged for using his helmet. The fine stems from a block on 49ers cornerback Deommodore Lenoir during George Pickens' 39-yard touchdown reception. Although officials initially flagged the play before picking up the penalty, the NFL reviewed the footage and determined that Lamb violated its helmet-use rules. That $23,882 figure is actually the biggest fine of the week, so it may be enough to convince Lamb to think twice before making that kind of play again. item.title: Trinity Rodman appears to injure shoulder, stays in NWSL Championship
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman went down clutching her left shoulder early in the 2026 NWSL Championship after a hard foul committed by the Kansas City Current on Saturday, Nov. 21. Current defender Laney Rouse collied with Rodman in the air at the five-minute mark of the championship game. Rodman remained down on the pitch in visible pain as a cascade of boos rained down from the home crowd at Audi Field. After a momentary delay, play continued as Rodman was tended to on the sidelines. After stretching her left arm and doing several arm circles, Rodman checked back into the game in the sixth minute to a loud applause, although she still appeared to be in some discomfort. The contact didn’t result in a card for Rouse, but the first yellow card of the game was handed out several minutes later when the Current’s Michelle Cooper was shown one for a hard foul on the Spirit’s Leicy Santos in the ninth minute. NWSL Championship live: Washington Spirit vs. Kansas City Current score, highlights Rodman has dealt with numerous injuries throughout her star-studded career, particularly in the Spirit's past two championship game appearances, which resulted in losses for Washington in 2024 and 2025. Rodman played through a sprained MCL in her right knee in the Spirit's 1-0 loss to Gotham FC in 2025, while a lingering back issue impacted her performance in the Spirit's 1-0 loss to the Orlando Pride in 2024. After being limited to a career-low 17 matches last season due to back and knee injuries, she bounced back with a career year this season that included personal highs in both goals (14), assists (10) and games played (33). "It makes me want to cry," Rodman said. "Just being able to be available, I don't think people realize how much of a blessing it is to be healthy enough to play. And I don't think you realize that until you go through something where it keeps you from doing something you love to do." item.title: Messi, Miami stunned by Columbus in MLS playoff opener
item.description: Columbus Crew's Gonzalo Tapia celebrates after scoring his second goal in a 3-0 win over Lionel Messi's Inter Miami (JC Ruiz) Lionel Messi's bid to win back-to-back MLS Cup titles suffered a blow on Saturday as 10-man Inter Miami were thumped 3-0 at home by Columbus Crew in their first-round playoff series opener. Two goals from Chile international Gonzalo Tapia either side of a Taha Habroune second-half strike secured a deserved victory for Crew in front of a shellshocked crowd at Miami's Nu Stadium. The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday. On Saturday's evidence, Columbus will head into game two confident of finishing the job after tearing Miami to shreds. The 24-year-old Tapia was a menace throughout, winning an early penalty after being brought down by Miami goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair before stepping up to convert the spot-kick. Miami's task got harder in the 36th minute when Gonzalo Lujan was sent off after receiving a second yellow card for a reckless late challenge on the Crew's Stephen Moreira. Columbus's US international goalkeeper Patrick Schulte, meanwhile, thwarted Miami's attempts to get back in the game, including one diving save to deny Messi a trademark free-kick. Messi was fortunate to escape dismissal on half-time, when he appeared to direct a throw-in into Tapia's face at point-blank range as frustrations boiled over. Columbus made the game safe early in the second half with two goals in six minutes. A fine flowing counter-attack ended with Harbroune coolly slotting past St.Clair in the 52nd minute before Tapia made it 3-0 in the 58th minute, punishing slack marking by Miami's Yannick Bright to go clean through on goal. "It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards. "We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added. "There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character." In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener. The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday. US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia. Miller’s 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring. item.description: Carlie Cisneros (12) — TUCSON, ARIZ. -- Volleyball vs. Grand Canyon University at McKale Center at ALKEME Arena. Aug. 19, 2026. | Photo by Marison Bilagody / Arizona Athletics The Arizona Wildcats have taken sets off or played very competitive three-setters against teams ranked 10th, 11th, 14th, and 32nd in the RPI during Big 12 play. On Saturday, No. 40 Utah was on the schedule. Once again, it was a competitive match that ended in a 3-1 (25-18, 22-25, 25-21, 26-24) loss. “Other than how we started off the set, the first set—I wasn’t too happy with that—I thought we did a good job of staying competitive on the floor,” Arizona head coach Rita Stubbs said. “Unfortunately, our skills broke down in certain situations, and coachability wasn’t necessarily the best, and they took advantage of it at the right time, but the wrong time for us.” Arizona was especially done in by Utah runs later in sets. That was even the case in the second set, which the Wildcats won. UA went up 19-12 in the second only to have the Utes go on a five-point run to close the lead to two. The big cushion was the saving grace for the Wildcats. They were able to trade points and mini-runs with Utah down the stretch to win by three points. Those mid- and late-set runs were their downfall in the third and fourth sets. It didn’t take a lot in sets that were so closely contested. The difference in the third came with the teams tied at 12. Utah went on a three-point run to reach the technical timeout leading 15-12. It never trailed again. Another three-point run later in the set gave the Utes set point at 24-19. Arizona saved two set points, but it was just one of five occasions when it scored more than one point in a row. Four of those five “runs” were of just two points and the other was three. The fourth was a back-and-forth affair throughout as Arizona fought to stay in the match. The Wildcats took their first lead at 7-6 and had a four-point lead at the technical timeout. As was common throughout the match, the timeout helped the team that had been struggling. Utah used a 7-2 run to take the lead at 18-17. Stubbs called time and Arizona responded with a 4-0 run to go up 21-17. The Wildcats were so close to evening the match. Once again, the timeout changed the teams’ fortunes. The Utes called time and followed with a 3-0 run to tie the set again. Arizona couldn’t string points together after that. The Utes had two 2-0 mini-runs. item.title: 'Baltimore isn't a talking point to me': Carmelo Anthony calls out Marlon Humphrey
item.description: Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images, Brad Penner-Imagn Images Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey made the wrong kind of headlines this past week after making a joke on his podcast at the expense of the city he represents on the field. During an episode of his podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show , Humphrey was asked what Baltimore was best at making, and responded, “criminals,” with a laugh. Given that Humphrey has played for the Ravens for a decade, the remark quickly made the rounds as fans and media alike expressed their disappointment. Humphrey has since apologized, but was sent home for the week by the team and will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers as a punishment for the comments. He has also been on the receiving end of critiques from the likes of Shannon Sharpe and Kevin Wildes , who suggested maybe it was time for him to stop podcasting. On Friday, former NBA star and current analyst Carmelo Anthony joined the voices of those calling out Humphrey. Anthony, who played his high school basketball in the Baltimore area, sent a clear message to Humphrey via a series of posts to his Instagram account. “Listen. I’ve been sitting with this one for a couple of days, because Baltimore isn’t a talking point to me. It’s my blood,” Anthony wrote. “I came up on Myrtle Avenue in West Baltimore. I saw what this city can take from you. I lost friends to the streets, and I watched people I loved get swallowed by a system that was built to swallow them. I know the reputation. I’ve heard every joke and every headline my whole life. “So when one of our own stands on our name and says the best thing Baltimore makes is criminals, and then laughs that it’ll get cut out, that doesn’t get cut out for me. It doesn’t get cut out for the kid in Baltimore who heard it. It doesn’t get cut out for the mother working two jobs to keep her son off the corner. And it doesn’t get cut out for the man who did his time, came home, and is fighting every day to be seen as more than his worst moment.” Anthony acknowledged Humphrey’s apology, but challenged him to get more involved in the local community and engage with the city and its people. “You don’t get to rep Baltimore on Sunday and talk about it like an outsider on Wednesday,” he wrote. Anthony closed out his message by asking that Humphrey make good on an invitation that Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott made to him to meet with residents who are working to make the city a better place and keep others from making the mistakes of their past. item.description: Michigan tight end Jalen Hoffman (42) makes a catch for the game-winning 2-point conversion against UCLA during the third overtime at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. ANN ARBOR, Mich. — UCLA traveled to Ann Arbor searching for a historic win. A victory would secure the program's first 11-win season, tie the school mark for single-season conference victories and clinch a berth in the Big Ten championship game. All UCLA had to do was defeat Michigan in The Big House. Instead, the fourth-ranked Bruins walked off the turf in defeat for the first time this season, falling to the Wolverines 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday at Michigan Stadium. “This was a battle, and obviously we came up a little bit short," head coach Bob Chesney said postgame. "We have to find a way to get better, period." Not only did UCLA watch a chance at an undefeated season and a potential trip to Indianapolis slip away in heartbreaking fashion, it also lost its starting quarterback. After marching down the field on a 15-play, 77-yard drive to tie the game with 10 seconds remaining on a jump-pass touchdown from Anthony Woods to Brayden Loftin, UCLA headed to overtime deadlocked at 10, looking to add another chapter to a remarkable campaign. On the first snap of overtime, senior quarterback Ty Dieffenbach scrambled to his right and was brought down by Michigan defender Troy Bowles for a 6-yard gain. Dieffenbach remained down on the play, appearing in serious pain before being carted off the field. item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day walks on the field during warmups before the game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Ohio State’s defense has been at the center of the Buckeyes’ disastrous season, and Saturday’s 31-28 loss at Nebraska may have been its worst performance yet. Now, the spotlight is on defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, the highest-paid coordinator in college football. After the game, head coach Ryan Day was asked whether he still had faith in Patricia. Day didn’t offer a vote of confidence, but he made it clear that no changes will be made until after next week’s game against Michigan, when Ohio State will “evaluate everything.” From Best to Bust Patricia’s first season as Ohio State’s defensive coordinator couldn’t have gone much better. The Buckeyes allowed the fewest points and yards per game of any defense in 14 years, and Ohio State rewarded him with a new three-year contract worth an average of $3.8 million per year, making him the highest-paid coordinator in college football. But the defense lost four All-Americans from that unit, and this season has been a different story. The defense has come up short in all four of Ohio State’s losses. Ohio State blew a 23-3 fourth-quarter lead in a 24-23 loss at Texas in Week 2. The Buckeyes then gave up 30 points in a loss at USC and 41 points in a blowout home loss to Oregon, the most they’d allowed in a game since 2022. After the Oregon loss, the Buckeyes fired special teams coordinator Robby Discher , while former players called for Day to “ clean house .” On Saturday, Nebraska, which hadn’t scored more than 17 points against a team with a winning record all season, put up 31. The Huskers ran for 176 yards, and Ohio State forced just two punts with zero takeaways. With each loss, it’s becoming fair to wonder whether Patricia’s success last season had more to do with the elite talent on his defense than his scheme. And Ohio State didn’t make him the highest-paid coordinator in the country to field a mediocre defense. Moving on from Patricia wouldn’t be cheap. item.description: DaRon Bland #26 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty It’s not a major surprise to find that Dallas Cowboys cornerback DaRon Bland has landed on the injured reserve with a high ankle sprain. The team had indicated it would be a multiple-week injury, and the Cowboys need all the roster spots they can muster. But for Bland, the injury could be something more significant–it could end his career as a Cowboy. It would, of course, be a sad end for a player who made waves in 2023 when he earned an NFL All-Pro nod for intercepting nine passes and returning five for touchdowns. It was a brilliant season for Bland, who appeared to be developing into a star after five interceptions in 2022, his rookie year. Not bad for a fifth-round pick out of Fresno State. But then, Bland hurt his foot in 2024. The team was still confident enough in him to five him a four-year, $92 million extension, but that proved ill-advised. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
